title: A Sinkhole Swallowed a 3-Storey Building in Guatemala City

scenes.text: A hole opened in a city street and swallowed a three-storey building.
Guatemala City, 2010. A tropical storm had just dumped days of rain.
Then the ground gave way. A perfect circle, 65 feet across. A factory dropped straight in.
Officials said 100 feet deep. Geologists said 300. Nobody saw the bottom.
The city sits on loose volcanic ash. A burst sewer pipe had been washing it away.
The workers had gone home an hour earlier. Three years before, another hole nearby killed three people.

description:
On 30 May 2010, after Tropical Storm Agatha, a near-perfect circular sinkhole about 20 metres (65 feet) across opened in Guatemala City and swallowed a three-storey clothing factory and an intersection.
Authorities put its depth at about 30 metres; geologists quoted by National Geographic estimated up to 100 metres. The city sits on loose volcanic pumice, and a leaking sewer pipe had been eroding it from below. Factory workers had left about an hour before.
Would you stay in a city built on volcanic ash? Comment below.
first_comment: Technically it is not a sinkhole at all, since there is no limestone; geologists call it a piping feature. Would you rather face an earthquake or a sinkhole?
